identity.name: Split-Seconds Chronograph
identity.one_liner: The 41mm platinum split-seconds chronograph with a blue enamel dial — the first Patek in-house column-wheel split-seconds (CHR 29-535 PS, 2010 caliber) and the most-cited modern Patek chronograph at the $200,000 price point.

narrative.story: The 5370P is the modern replacement for the 5004P. The CHR 29-535 PS caliber is the first Patek in-house column-wheel chronograph with a split-seconds mechanism; the column wheel is visible through the case back. The 41mm platinum case, the blue enamel dial, and the two-level sub-dial layout are the visual signature. The 5370P is the most-cited modern Patek grand complication chronograph and the watch a collector cites when arguing Patek's chronograph engineering is at the top of the Swiss industry.
narrative.collector_notes: The 5370P is the first Patek chronograph with a blue enamel dial; enamel is one of the most fragile dial-making processes and is hand-fired at 800°C.
